text: Reacher was eating breakfast when the police came for him.
He had walked into Margrave with no car, no bag, and no plan to stay.
Reacher saw them first.
The door opened hard, and the room changed.
Forks stopped moving.
Coffee cups paused halfway to mouths.
Small towns knew when trouble had walked in.
Reacher could live with that.
They told him to stand.
Reacher stood slowly, because fast movement made nervous men more nervous.
They had found Reacher.
At the station, they tried to make him small.
They put him in a room, shut the door.
This was bad police work, dressed up in uniforms.
They wanted Reacher to explain why he was in town.
They wanted him to explain why a man was dead.
They wanted him to explain why a stranger with no local ties had shown up at the same time.
Reacher let them talk.
Better men had still been wrong.
The room was locked, but Reacher did not feel trapped.
He watched the men move.
The mistake was theirs.
They moved Reacher from the interview room to a cell.
That was their next mistake.
It usually did.
The men inside the holding area looked him over.
They saw a stranger, tall and quiet, brought in by local police.
Some men see quiet and think weak.
That mistake could cost a man.
Reacher went back to the wall.
Nobody else stepped close.
That was the first smart thing anyone had done all day.
Reacher was not prey.
Margrave thought it had handled the stranger.
It had not handled him.
Now he was interested.
Reacher began putting the pieces together.
The arrest had been too quick.
The questions had been too eager.
The men in charge acted less like officers hunting truth.
He had been trained to find the weak point.
The diner was where they first saw him.
It was not where this would end.
They had invited it in.
